content: QR-code indoor navigation is documented as a point-fix, hardware-free positioning method: printed codes at entrances, decision points, elevators, lobbies and information desks act as position anchors. Navigine (Dec 2024) describes the flow: scan QR, app opens a digital map with that location as origin, user picks a POI from a list, the system produces a short route that prioritises the most suitable elevators, entrances and hallways and can offer routes avoiding narrow stairs or steep climbs. ExpoFP (Aug 2026) and the Zapworks guide both state QR wayfinding does NOT continuously track a user; each scan establishes a known starting point, and QR codes keep working offline once the map is cached. Vendor docs also show per-location QR download from an admin panel (3D Wayfinder) and QR codes used on signs and placards at elevators and lobbies (WayfindingPro).
